subject: Partitioned measurement proposal for hosted API p50/p95 commitments
messages:
From: Samir Khatri <samir@opticai.com>

Cc: Alyssa Reed <alyssa@opticai.com>

Subject: Hosted API SLOs — proposal for partitioned measurement windows

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Before we get the SOW signed, OpticAI needs tighter language about how you measure p50/p95 for the hosted API. Our traffic pattern has regular baseline queries and unpredictable burst days tied to product launches; a single rolling window makes it hard for us to forecast risk.

Can you share a proposal for "partitioned" measurement windows (e.g., baseline vs peak-day vs canary) and how exceptions would be handled (temporary carveouts, holiday events, canary phases)? Specifically:
- What are Redwood's default p50/p95 numbers and measurement windows for hosted customers?
- How would you define and signal a temporary carveout (who owns the trigger and evidence)?
- Can we get an optional regional carveout for our APAC launches for the first 90 days?

We want to avoid an overly broad exception clause, but need operational levers so our product team can plan. Attaching a one-page sketch of our traffic cadence.

Best,
Samir

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — proposal for partitioned measurement windows

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic sketch. Below is a proposal we can fold into the SOW as an amendment:

1) Baseline commitments (default hosted profile)
- p50: <= 60ms (in-region, median request-to-first-token)
- p95: <= 320ms (in-region, end-to-end generation)
- Measurement: rolling 30-day window, sampled at 100% for billing customers (aggregated per region)

2) Partitioned measurement windows (new, opt-in model)
- Baseline window: rolling 30-day as above (captures day-to-day steady state)
- Peak-day window: discrete 24-hour slices flagged by customer or Redwood (used only to identify transient deviation; not counted against baseline SLOs unless persistent for >14 days)
- Canary window: first 7 days after go-live or model swap; Redwood applies a warmup carveout for the first 72 hours of a canary to avoid warm caches skewing numbers

3) Temporary carveout process (proposal)
- Trigger: customer opens a carveout request in the Console (or our CS team files on their behalf) with an explicit start/end time and justification (e.g., marketing launch, data migration)
- Evidence: traffic patterns and spike correlation, request IDs, and expected end time; Redwood may require a short-run log sample (we provide a checklist)
- Decisioning: Redwood operations reviews within 48 hours; approved carveouts are applied retroactively to the flagged window but not to baseline unless extension requested

4) Regional exceptions
- OpticAI can request a time-limited APAC carveout for the first 90 days of regional launch; this is treated as a standard temporary carveout with higher scrutiny and an operations playbook (we recommend a staggered rollout with canary traffic)

5) Canaries & fallback
- During canaries, Redwood will enable fallback to a smaller model variant on overload; fallbacks are recorded and surfaced in the Console (noted in SLO evidence).

Next steps if this looks reasonable:
- Ben (cc'd) will add operational notes and sample evidence we require.
- If agreed, we attach an amendment to the SOW (I can send a draft).

Quick note: I'll attach the SLO amendment draft and an internal checklist for carveout evidence.

Thanks,
Monica

Samir / Monica — quick technical clarifications and operational guardrails from the infra side:

- Measurement sampling: we track 100% of production tokens for hosts on our paid tier; for partitioned windows we tag each request with a "window" label (baseline|peak|canary) to keep aggregation orthogonal.
- Warmup carveout: 72-hour window is applied per-model-per-region. Warmup detection looks for KV cache miss rates and increased cold-starts; we log this and include the traces with the carveout evidence.
- Peak-day detection: customer-flagged windows win; if Redwood observes an anomaly we open a warning ticket and propose a provisional peak-day label pending evidence.
- P95 calculation: we use request-complete latencies with upstream routing time included; network transit outside Redwood-managed regions is excluded when calculating in-region commitments (we will document the exact boundary in the SOW).

Operational note: for holiday or marketing spikes, OpticAI should file the carveout at least 24 hours in advance if possible; emergency retroactive requests are allowed but require stronger evidence.

I attached the evidence checklist Monica mentioned — it lists the log slices, trace IDs, and synthetic test patterns we typically need.

-ben

Thanks, Monica and Ben — helpful level of detail. A couple of quick asks before we mark this as accepted to the SOW:
- Can Redwood add a clause that peak-day windows <48 hours will not be counted against baseline SLOs unless they repeat more than twice in a 30-day rolling period?
- We'll likely need an APAC carveout for our launch on 2026-11-05; can you pre-approve a 90-day window with the understanding we'll provide evidence and run canary traffic for 7 days?

If you can add those two items to the draft SOW, we'll circulate internally and push for signature. We'll want DocuSign and the HubSpot deal updated so our procurement team can route the approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the draft.

Best,
Samir
